page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-lc1m2.small is an entry-level, shared-core burstable virtual machine hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture, drawing compute power from a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor. The virtual machine configuration provides 1 burstable vCPU mapped to a single physical core, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory. Advanced CPU instruction flags are present, including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, or complimentary public IPv4 networking allocations, and it operates with a 0 Gbps network baseline.

Benchmark evaluation across standard compute and memory suites indicates minimal baseline throughput consistent with a shared single-core resource tier. Synthetic CPU performance measures 1042.98 in both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests. Large-block uncached memory operations register 8.7 GB/s read throughput and 7.34 GB/s write throughput. For operational services, Redis achieves 1.12 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 0.86 GB/s. In micro-workload machine learning tests, inference throughput using a small 135M parameter language model reaches 53.79 tokens per second for prompt ingestion and 9.43 tokens per second for text generation.

Because the vCPU is subject to burstable resource allocation, sustained high compute utilization risks core throttling. From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance provides economical resource density for micro-scale operational tasks where idle periods predominate. Tradeoffs include low baseline processing capacity, zero bundled local storage, and the absence of hardware redundancy. The instance is positioned for low-traffic dev-test sandboxes, internal staging environments, small batch cron executions, and lightweight background automation scripts.
